Title: Mother braves flames thrice, but fails to save son from house fire
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A mother braved raging flames three times in a desperate attempt to wake her sleeping son, but the rescue attempt ended in tragedy when he was found dead in a house fire at Kampung Gong Tok Nasek here, late last night.
In the 10.50pm incident, Sharipah Yusof, 59, said she and her husband, Abd Rashid Md Zain, 64, were asleep downstairs, while her eldest son, Abd Latif Abd Rashid, 41, was sleeping alone in an upstairs bedroom.
She said she only realised the danger after hearing shouts from members of the public alerting her to the fire and urging her to escape.
"At first, I thought someone had come to the house. When I opened the bedroom door, I was shocked to see flames already raging on the upper floor as well as several parts of the ground floor. I immediately went outside as the fire grew larger.
"Bystanders rescued my husband. After getting out of the house, I suddenly remembered my son was sleeping upstairs. I immediately went back inside to wake him," she said when met at the scene last night.
Sharipah said she braved the fire three times while knocking on her son's bedroom door, which was locked from the inside, but received no response.
"The first and second times, I was still able to go inside while calling out to him repeatedly. The third time, I tried to enter but could not because the fire was too big and the heat was overwhelming.
"When the firefighters arrived, I immediately told them that my son was upstairs," she said.
According to Sharipah, Abd Latif, the eldest of four siblings, was a person with learning disabilities (OKU) who had not left the house for a long time.
She said that over the past few days, her son had lost his appetite, remained quiet, and spent most of his time confined to his room.
"Everything in the house, including clothes, furniture, electrical items, and my husband's identification documents, was destroyed in the fire," she said.
Meanwhile, the victim's younger sister, Asiah, 40, said she received a phone call from her younger brother informing her that their parents' house was on fire, before rushing over from her home in Kampung Setar Kanan, Marang.
"I was already asleep when my brother called to tell me our mother's house was on fire. I rushed over with my husband.
"Throughout the journey, I prayed that my brother, mother, and father were safe, as only the three of them lived there. However, when I arrived, I was devastated to learn that my brother was trapped in his bedroom," she said.
Asiah said the last time she saw the victim was about a month ago when she took him to seek medical treatment.
"At that time, my brother told me he felt uneasy, as if someone was calling out to him. So my husband and I took him for treatment.
"He also wanted to get a new pair of spectacles because his eyesight was worsening, but that wish was never fulfilled. I did not expect that to be our last meeting," she said.

Title: Democratic-led US states sue in latest challenge to Trump's tariffs
Article:
WASHINGTON: Twenty-five US states, nearly all led by Democrats, sued Donald Trump's administration on Monday over wide-ranging tariffs, arguing that the president had exceeded his authority in imposing the new levies on dozens of countries.
The states filed suit at the US Court of International Trade in New York, asking judges to halt the implementation of the tariffs, declare them unlawful and order the government to issue refunds.
"There is no rational fit between the purported problem of forced labour in international supply chains and the blanket global tariffs the USTR imposed," the coalition of states argued in a court filing, referring to the US Trade Representative's office.
The challenge is related to Trump's latest round of tariffs of between 10 and 12.5 per cent imposed against 60 trading partners — forming the bulk of US imports — last month.
The tariffs were imposed after probes by the USTR's office into allegations of "forced labour", conducted under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.
Since taking office for his second term, Trump has upended global trade by imposing wide-ranging tariffs — at sometimes eye-watering levels — against Washington's friends and foes alike.
Trump has argued that US trading partners have been taking advantage of the world's largest economy, and has sought to use tariffs as leverage to strike new trade deals.
On Monday, the White House hit back at the latest challenge to Trump's tariffs, arguing that the government's move was legal.
"The United States is using its lawful authority to obtain the elimination of unreasonable acts, policies, and practices that burden US commerce," said Kush Desai, a White House spokesperson, in a statement.
"Section 301 tariffs have proven to be a legally durable tool since the President's first term, and they remain so now."
[[nid:1503655]]
EARLIER CHALLENGES
Trump's first round of tariffs, imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, was struck down by the US Supreme Court in February.
He replaced those with a 10 per cent global levy, which expired in July.
The new Section 301 tariffs replaced that levy, taking effect as the 10 per cent tariff expired on July 24.
Of the 25 states in the suit, 23 have Democratic governors while two — Nevada and Vermont — are led by Republicans.
In their court filing, the states argued that the Section 301 probes were "a pretextual and unlawful effort to exert unfettered tariff power".
The document lays out a timeline of Trump administration officials' statements, arguing that the investigations were rushed and prejudged when they were initiated.
"The Tariff Action is arbitrary, capricious, and contrary to law," the complaint says.
"The plaintiff states oppose forced labour in all its forms and support protections for workers around the globe. But the Administration cannot use forced labour as a pretext to continue its illegal tariff scheme."
Trump's separate sector-specific tariffs — imposed under different legal authorities on steel, automobiles and other goods — have been unaffected by recent legal challenges.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Maran Umno Youth chief, three family members buried in one grave
Article:
MARAN: Maran Umno Youth chief Mohd Radzi Rahimi and three of his family members, who tragically lost their lives after a large tree fell onto their pick-up truck in Bentong yesterday, were laid to rest in a single grave today.
The four victims — Radzi, his wife, Nuraini Mohammad Jafri, 36, their five-year-old son, Rizz Hazim, and Radzi's brother-in-law, Mohammad Nizam Mohammad Jafri, 34 — were buried at the Sri Chedung Muslim cemetery here about 3.15am.
Despite the early hour, a large crowd of relatives, friends and politicians gathered at the cemetery to pay their final respects.
Earlier, after post-mortem examinations were completed at the Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital forensic unit in Temerloh about 11.30pm, the bodies were taken to the Kampung Paya Luas Mosque in Temerloh to be bathed and shrouded.
Funeral prayers were then held at the Asy-Syakirin Mosque in Maran before the victims were laid to rest.
In the 12.30pm incident, Radzi, Nuraini, Rizz Hazim and Mohammad Nizam, who was driving the pick-up truck, were
killed on the spot
. Rizz Hazim's twin brother, Muhammad Rizz Haziq, survived with injuries.
Radzi and his family were returning from Genting Highlands when
the incident occurred
along the old Kuala Lumpur-Bentong Road in Janda Baik.

Title: First 2 deaths reported in US Cyclosporiasis outbreak
Article:
LOS ANGELES: The US Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) on Monday confirmed the first two deaths linked to the country's cyclosporiasis outbreak, Xinhua reported.
"CDC is aware of two cyclosporiasis-related deaths in people with underlying health conditions from Michigan as part of this outbreak," the CDC said in a notice, adding that it will update its website to include laboratory-confirmed cases, hospitalisations and deaths.
According to the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services, medical records indicate that both individuals had significant underlying health conditions that may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration.
State health officials said no additional information about the two cases would be released.
However, they emphasised that cyclosporiasis is generally not life-threatening and that deaths associated with the illness are rare in the United States.
The department said it is continuing to investigate the outbreak in the state.
"While the investigation is ongoing, available information indicates that lettuce or salad greens may be a potential source of this outbreak.
"However, other food items cannot be completely ruled out. No specific type of produce, grower, or supplier has been identified as the source," it said. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, nearly unchanged against greenback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against other major currencies, and was almost unchanged versus the US dollar on Tuesday following the release of the US Institute for Supply Management (ISM) Manufacturing PMI data.
At 8am, the local currency was little changed against the greenback at 4.0935/1000  from Monday's close of 4.0935/0975.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US ISM Manufacturing PMI surprised on the upside as the index rose to 55.6 points in July from the consensus estimate of 54.0 points, reinforcing expectations of a US interest rate hike.

Title: Cargo vessel hit by 'unknown projectile' in Hormuz Strait
Article:
DUBAI: A cargo vessel was struck by an "unknown projectile" in the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Oman, a British maritime agency said on Tuesday, without providing details on damage or injuries.
The vessel, which has not been named, reported being "hit by an unknown projectile", and authorities were investigating, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said.
The incident occurred 20 nautical miles (37 kilometres) northeast of Al Khasab, Oman.

Title: WHO demands protection for Gaza health care facilities amid israeli attacks
Article:
GAZA CITY: The World Health Organisation (WHO) called on Monday for an immediate end to Israeli attacks on medical facilities in Gaza following a strike that destroyed a critical storage unit and essential supplies.
"WHO calls for the protection of health care. Health care facilities must never be attacked or militarised," Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said in a statement, according to Anadolu Ajansi.
Over the weekend, an Israeli attack targeted a storage site adjacent to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, damaging the main building and destroying medical equipment, including items recently delivered by the WHO.
Ghebreyesus noted that despite an existing ceasefire, insecurity remains high in the enclave as residents struggle with malnutrition, disease and a lack of medical care.
Gaza's Health Ministry warned Saturday that the destruction of the drug warehouse at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital has pushed the enclave's medical system to the brink of collapse.
Since October 2023, the WHO has recorded nearly 1,000 attacks on health care in Gaza, resulting in more than 1,000 deaths and 1,700 injuries.
Israel has killed more than 73,000 people and injured over 174,000 others in a brutal war in Gaza since October 2023.
Despite a ceasefire agreement in effect since Oct 10, 2025, Israel has continued its attacks across the enclave, killing 1,250 Palestinians and injuring 4,110 others, according to Gaza's Health Ministry. — BERNAMA
TAGS: WHO, Gaza, health facility, protection, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus

Title: Identity politics claims just an excuse to hide defeat, Khaled tells PH leaders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A senior Umno leader has dismissed claims by Pakatan Harapan leaders suggesting that the Negri Sembilan election campaign was marred by racial identity politics.
Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin told the New Straits Times that such claims were merely an excuse by PH leaders to cover up their defeat in the Aug 1 state election.
"I think that is an excuse to cover up the defeat.
"The call for Malays to unite and the consolidation of the ummah are not racist. In fact, they are something that Malays have been yearning for.
"BN also fielded non-Malay candidates from MCA and MIC. Which statements made by BN leaders during the campaign could be considered racist?"
He added that some parties simply did not want unity and consolidation among Malays to happen.
"As such, they label such efforts as racist. As long as Umno exists, we will continue to protect and defend the welfare of all people in the country," he said.
Parti Wawasan Negara information chief Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal concurred with Khaled, describing PH leaders' assessment of the election outcome as a lazy analysis.
The Machang member of Parliament also claimed that such statements were intended to divert attention from what he described as the real issue, namely a deficit of trust among voters towards PH.
"How could PN and BN score such a handsome victory in the Negri Sembilan polls? For a simple reason, the majority of Malays want to see Malaysians united. And it has to start with unity among Malay political parties," he said.
PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said people, especially non-Malays, should not fear the political understanding reached between BN and PN, as seen in the Negri Sembilan and Johor elections.
"BN has experience governing the country for many years, while Pas has governed Kelantan for more than 30 years.
"There has been no threat to the non-Malay community in the state. Many people are quick to criticise the situation without ever setting foot in Kelantan," said Tuan Ibrahim, who is also Pas deputy president.
In the Negri Sembilan election last Saturday, BN formed the state government with Perikatan Nasional after securing 25 seats, while PH won 11 seats.
Since then, several PH leaders, including the coalition's election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Amanah deputy president and election director Datuk Seri Mujahid Yusof Rawa, have attributed the defeat to what they described as the influence of racial identity politics.
"While we respect the voters' decision, we are also concerned that parties promoting narrow racial and religious identity narratives risk pushing the political climate towards greater volatility," Mujahid said in a statement yesterday.
Mujahid also criticised BN, PH's partner in the federal unity government, over its cooperation with PN during the state election.

Title: Two Pakistanis arrested in joint Singapore-Pakistan-Interpol cybercrime operation
Article:
SINGAPORE: Two Pakistani nationals linked to the Tycoon2FA cybercrime syndicate were arrested in Pakistan following a joint operation by the Singapore Police Force (SPF), Pakistan's National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) and Interpol.
In a statement on Monday, the SPF said Tycoon2FA is a phishing-as-a-service platform that provides subscribers with ready-made phishing infrastructure for a monthly fee, enabling cybercriminals to create fake websites to steal victims' credentials and gain unauthorised access to their accounts.
The platform has been linked to more than 96,000 phishing victims worldwide.
"There were at least three cases reported in Singapore between November 2025 and January 2026, where business email accounts were compromised despite the use of multi-factor authentication," the statement read.
The SPF said officers from its Cyber Command worked closely with the NCCIA and Interpol after investigating the cases, leading to the identification of the two Pakistani nationals believed to have developed Tycoon2FA.
Acting on the intelligence, the NCCIA arrested the suspects on June 25 and July 1 for offences under Pakistan's Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016.
Authorities also seized a laptop, two central processing units and six mobile devices during the operation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KTMB extends Southern Shuttle service to Paloh from Aug 8
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) will extend its Southern Shuttle service on the Paloh-JB Sentral-Paloh route from Aug 8.
KTMB said in a statement today that the expanded service will cover seven stations – Paloh, Kluang, Renggam, Layang-Layang, Kulai, Kempas Baru and JB Sentral – with the journey from Paloh to JB Sentral taking about 120 minutes.
According to KTMB, the extension is a strategic initiative by the Transport Ministry (MOT) to provide a direct rail link between suburban areas and the key economic hubs of Kulai and JB Sentral.
"The expansion, implemented less than three months after the initial phase, will traverse the central Johor corridor by utilising part of the Gemas-Johor Bahru Electrified Double-Track Project (PLBEGJB) alignment.
"This initiative reflects the Government's and KTMB's ongoing commitment to enhancing public mobility through wider access to rail services," the statement said.
KTMB said the new service will operate 10 trips daily, comprising five services from Paloh to JB Sentral and five in the opposite direction, with each train accommodating up to 400 passengers.
The earliest service from Paloh will depart at 3.55am and arrive at JB Sentral at 5.52am, while the last train from JB Sentral will leave at 8.30pm and reach Paloh at 10.27pm.
"The early morning and evening schedules are designed to support the needs of daily commuters, including workers continuing their journey to Singapore via the Johor Bahru border crossing," the statement said.
KTMB said connecting services will also be available at Kempas Baru Station, allowing passengers to transfer to the Kempas Baru-Pasir Gudang-Kempas Baru route, thereby strengthening connectivity between the Paloh-Kluang-Kulai-Johor Bahru corridor and the Pasir Gudang industrial area.
Meanwhile, promotional fares for the Southern Shuttle service will remain in place until new electric trains are delivered, with the Paloh-JB Sentral fare reduced from RM15.30 to a promotional one-way fare of RM7.70.
KTMB also said the MyRailLife Pass will be extended to cover the Southern Shuttle service from Aug 8 to Dec 31, offering free travel for children aged four to six, students from Year One to Form Six, and persons with disabilities (PwDs), subject to terms and conditions.
Since its introduction, the Southern Shuttle service has recorded 3,209 passengers on its two initial routes, reflecting an encouraging public response to a more convenient and comfortable rail transport option.
KTMB said the service expansion is expected to support workforce mobility, economic activities and the development of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), while helping to reduce reliance on private vehicles.

Title: [UPDATED] Five more Immigration officers arrested over hacking of MyIMMs, fraudulent PLKS
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has arrested five more Immigration Department officers in the widening investigation into the alleged hacking of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to issue fraudulent approval of Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS).
The latest arrests are part of the ongoing Op Crack investigation, which has already seen several Immigration officers, company directors, foreigners and a police officer detained over alleged corruption and system breach.
An MACC source said the five suspects, four men and a woman aged in their 30s and 40s, were arrested about 1pm yesterday when they turned up to have their statements recorded at MACC headquarters.
Preliminary investigations found that all five officers were suspected of conspiring to hack the MyIMMs system while assisting in the approval of PLKS applications without complying with the proper procedures.
Following the arrests, investigators seized five mobile phones belonging to the suspects for forensic examination.
The source said MACC has so far recorded statements from 17 individuals to assist in the investigation.
Investigators have also frozen nine bank accounts, including four belonging to individuals and two registered to companies, involving approximately RM300,000.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests when contacted, adding that the case is being investigated under Sections 17(a) and 16(a) of the MACC Act 2009.
He said
all five suspects
would be brought before the Putrajaya magistrates's court  this morning for remand proceedings.
[[nid:1503633]]
Yesterday it was reported that a Myanmar woman suspected of acting as an illegal agent for a syndicate offering fraudulently issued Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) to undocumented foreign workers was arrested.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban had said the woman was among eight Myanmar citizens arrested during a special operation at a residential premises in Bandar Mahkota Cheras, Selangor, on Saturday.
The operation, which began at 3.50pm, was conducted by officers from the Intelligence and Special Operations Division at the Immigration Department headquarters in Putrajaya.
The raid was a follow-up to a joint operation conducted by the department and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission on July 28
Initial investigations found that
the woman had links to a Myanmar man
believed to be the mastermind of the syndicate, who was arrested by the MACC during Op Crack.
It was previously reported that a syndicate believed to have hacked the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to fraudulently process and approve PLKS passes was dismantled in a joint operation by the MACC and the Immigration Department.
A total of 12 people were arrested during the integrated operation, codenamed Op Crack.
Those detained comprised two company directors, three foreigners, four Immigration officers, two officers from the department's Information Technology Division, and a policeman.
The syndicate is believed to have exploited unused PLKS quotas dating back to 2011 to issue work passes without paying the required levy.

Title: TikTok settling three teen social media lawsuits ahead of trial
Article:
NEW YORK: TikTok has agreed to settle three lawsuits brought by young people who accuse social media companies of designing their platforms to be addictive and harming their mental health, a plaintiffs' lawyer said Monday.
The terms of the settlements are confidential and subject to the finalisation of written settlement agreements with TikTok, according to Joseph VanZandt, a lawyer for the plaintiffs.
TikTok did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The cases are among thousands of similar lawsuits consolidated in California state court. The plaintiffs' claims against Meta Platforms, Google's YouTube and Snap Inc's Snapchat will continue. A trial is scheduled in October.
The three cases, brought by plaintiffs identified only by their initials because they are minors, were selected as bellwether, or test, trials from among about 3,300 lawsuits before Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Carolyn Kuhl, who is overseeing consolidated claims that social media platforms are addictive and harm young users.
The companies have denied the allegations and say they take extensive steps to keep teens and young users safe on their platforms.
Attorneys often use bellwether verdicts to gauge how juries may view similar claims, helping them assess the potential value of remaining cases and guide settlement negotiations.
The plaintiffs who are settling with TikTok are S.J., a 15-year-old girl from Illinois who has alleged the social media platforms caused her to suffer from self-harm, anxiety, depression, addiction and an eating disorder; P.M.Y., a 15-year-old from New Jersey who has alleged addiction, depression and self-harm; and K.D.B., an 18-year-old from Mississippi who alleged that overuse of the platforms caused anxiety, depression, addiction, self-harm and an eating disorder, according to VanZandt.
The settlements come after another bellwether case ended before trial in July, when a teenage plaintiff dropped his claims against Meta after the other defendants settled.
The first trial in the litigation, which ended in March, resulted in a US$4.2 million verdict against Meta and a US$1.8 million one against Google in a case brought by a woman who said she became addicted to social media platforms at a young age because of their attention-grabbing design. TikTok and Snap settled that case before trial.
Another 2,600 cases making similar claims, brought by individuals, school districts, municipalities and states, are pending in California federal court.
In addition, nearly every state attorney general has sued social media companies in their own state courts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US State Department to close consulates in Canada, Japan and Indonesia, sources say
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US State Department has notified Congress that it plans to close five foreign missions in a rare downsizing of America's global diplomatic footprint, according to people familiar with the notice.
In the notice sent to some congressional committees late last week, the State Department said it planned to close its posts in St. George's, Grenada; Nagoya, Japan; Medan, Indonesia; Douala, Cameroon; and Winnipeg, Canada.
The people familiar with the notice spoke on condition of anonymity because the notice was not public.
The expected closures, which have not been previously reported, represent a rare example of the US closing multiple foreign missions in a downsizing that is not tied to a particular geopolitical event.
Early last year, during the opening months of the Trump administration, the State Department began preparations to shut down nearly a dozen foreign missions, Reuters and other media outlets reported at the time, as part of a broader push by the Republican president to transform the US bureaucracy so that it is fully aligned with his "America First" agenda.
The White House Office of Management and Budget had advocated for an even more ambitious closure programme, targeting up to 30 foreign missions.
Some administration officials have privately argued that some smaller foreign missions are inessential and not cost-effective.
Democrats and some former foreign policy and national security officials argue that cuts to the US diplomatic footprint – coupled with the dismantling of the US Agency for International Development, which provided billions of dollars' worth of aid globally – risk undermining American leadership, while leaving a dangerous vacuum for adversaries like China and Russia to fill.
While the State Department did undergo a broad bureaucratic overhaul last year – cutting dozens of bureaus and hundreds of staff – no foreign missions were shuttered.
Asked for comment on Sunday, the State Department issued a statement that did not confirm the closures but said it was focused on ensuring that the nation's diplomatic footprint was efficient and effective.
The department added that it was committed to following congressional notification procedures.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has portrayed cost-cutting measures as necessary to right-size an organisation many conservatives see as bloated and overly bureaucratic.
The US mission in St. George's, Grenada, is an embassy. The posts in Medan, Winnipeg and Nagoya are consulates, while the post in Douala is an "embassy branch office".
Consulates and branch offices typically represent US interests in regions outside a foreign country's capital city, where the US embassy is typically located.
During the administration of former President Joe Biden, the US government opened several foreign missions, all of them in the Pacific region, where the US is competing for influence with China.
While China does not have a functioning foreign mission in Douala or Winnipeg, it does have a diplomatic presence in St. George's, Nagoya and Medan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Spain defends Ceuta sovereignty after Moroccan migrant rush
Article:
CEUTA: Spain on Monday insisted its sovereignty over Ceuta was "unquestionable", after tens of thousands of migrants irregularly entered the North African territory from Morocco in an unprecedented and deadly surge.
Madrid has avoided criticising Rabat over last week's mass arrivals, which some commentators have interpreted as a means for Morocco to pressure Spain.
Morocco does not recognise Ceuta and Madrid's other territory in North Africa, Melilla, as Spanish and has claimed sovereignty over them since its independence in 1956.
Answering a question during televised remarks on Monday, Spain's Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares said: "That Ceuta and Melilla are an integral part of Spain's territory is unquestionable, for the whole world."
Most of the estimated 50,000 people who rushed into Ceuta – most having swum by sea around the border barrier – have since returned to Morocco.
The Spanish central government's delegate in Ceuta, Miguel Angel Perez, said Monday that 2,500 of them were estimated to still be in Ceuta.
Ceuta's top official Juan Jesus Vivas put the figure at between 3,000 and 5,000.
Dozens were enduring squalid conditions in a warehouse complex, including 29-year-old Nadia.
"We don't have water to wash or shower. The showers and toilets have been closed. Frankly, we're suffering terribly," the Moroccan told AFP.
Her compatriot, Asia, who had also reached Ceuta from Morocco, added: "There's dirt and mould. The toilets are filthy. Many people use them, and there aren't enough for everyone."
The charity Save the Children said "about 1,000" of the remaining migrants from last week's arrivals were minors who were "unprotected".
It said Ceuta's child protection system had capacity to look after just 100.
'LONG PROCESS'
Spanish authorities said the toll of 72 people found dead in their waters had not risen on Monday.
Of those, "first we have to identify them, which is the first big problem, because many of them came without any identification," said a source in the Spanish government delegation in Ceuta who asked not to be named.
"Then we have to find out who their families are" through the Moroccan authorities, the source added. "Then the bodies will have to be identified by the families. So it could be a long process."
Some analysts suggested Morocco might have allowed migrants to cross the border to put diplomatic pressure on Spain, which has recently improved ties with Rabat's arch-enemy Algeria.
Spanish officials accused criminal gangs of spreading rumours that a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling on immigration would allow migrants easier passage.
EU interior ministers scheduled a video call for Tuesday about the Ceuta migrant surge.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says Iran facing 'last chance before decapitation'
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that negotiations with Iran were ongoing despite Teheran's denials and that the Islamic republic was facing a "last chance before decapitation".
Trump, speaking to reporters at the White House, said he had agreed to continue pursuing talks with Iran at the request of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and other countries.
Iran's Foreign Ministry denied on Monday that negotiations with Washington were taking place, but Trump insisted they were. "We are talking right now," he said.
"This is a last chance for them to sign a good document," the US president added. "I want to give them every last chance before decapitation."
The talks are focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which Trump said could come "literally by tomorrow", and the denuclearisation of Iran, which he said could "take a little while".
Washington and Teheran have been at war since Feb 28, when the United States and Israel launched surprise strikes against Iran, although months of on-and-off diplomacy have led to periods of relative calm.
More than five months later, Iran remains able to fire missiles and drones at US and allied targets in the region and retains its enriched uranium stockpiles.
In what has become a familiar pattern, Trump last week threatened to hit Iran "very hard" — potentially with renewed attacks against energy infrastructure — only to pull back on Saturday, saying the "perimeters" of a deal were there.
Iran, for its part, said it was not currently negotiating with the United States.
"Our negotiations are with Oman to secure passage through the Strait of Hormuz," the critical oil corridor, Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said.
HORMUZ
Hormuz has been a major sticking point in efforts to end the war. Since a ceasefire broke down, Iran has reprised a blockade of the waterway that it first imposed early in the war, obstructing vessels attempting to pass and firing on commercial ships.
Calling Teheran "duplicitous" for "openly and proudly" saying it was not negotiating, Trump wrote on social media: "Whether Iran wants to admit it or not, we are, in fact, talking of a solution to a problem that they have caused, for decades."
He pointed to the United States' counter-blockade of Iranian ports, adding: "Nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a Deal, or Total Surrender, is accomplished."
Before the war, there was free passage through Hormuz, but Iran now insists on retaining control and charging fees, something the United States rejects.
Teheran has refused to let ships travel any route other than one that hugs the Iranian coast.
On Sunday, Baqaei told state television that a deal was close on managing Hormuz together with Oman, which sits on the other side of the narrow waterway.
"We are now going to reach an understanding on a route acceptable to both sides – neither the northern route nor the southern route – but one that respects the sovereign rights of both sides and safeguards our national interests and security," he said.
But he insisted that such an agreement did not mean the reopening of the strait.
On Sunday, a tanker off the coast of Oman reported hearing an explosion nearby, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Centre reported, but the ship and crew were all reported safe.
DENUCLEARISATION 'HAS TO HAPPEN'
The US president said at the start of the conflict that the war was necessary to deal with Iran's nuclear programme, and he repeated on Monday that "the denuclearisation of Iran has to happen".
Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, although Teheran insists the programme is entirely civilian in nature.
Speaking to reporters on Air Force One over the weekend, Trump said he had been asked by Iran as well as regional US partners to hold off on further strikes, which he claimed would have been "the biggest attack since World War II".
Iranian media denied that Teheran had asked Trump not to strike.
A previous ceasefire deal fell through last month. It was supposed to open the Strait of Hormuz to ships carrying vital energy exports from the Gulf to feed the global economy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: North Korea condemns US and allies' cyber threat warning
Article:
SEOUL: North Korea accused the United States and its allies of seeking to "tarnish the image" of the communist state after they warned against employing its IT workers, state media reported on Tuesday.
The US and 10 Asian and European allies on Friday issued a joint statement saying North Korea was using skilled workers under false identities to fund its nuclear and ballistic missile programmes.
An unnamed spokesman for the North Korean Foreign Ministry dismissed the joint warning as "a stereotyped political accusation with a sinister purpose to tarnish the image of our state", state news agency KCNA reported.
"It is illogical that the US, which has possessed and operated the biggest cyber force in the world by monopolising the core resources of cyberspace, is talking about 'cyber threat' from other countries. And it is a mere excuse for justifying its illegal policy of placing pressure on sovereign states," the spokesman added.
Friday's alert from the US and its allies said North Korean IT workers were impersonating nationals of other countries to obtain work and income on online platforms, and remit the money to government agencies.
It warned that North Korean workers were using AI tools to further obscure their true identities.
North Korea faces a slew of international sanctions over its weapons and nuclear programmes. It is believed to operate widespread cybercrime, cryptocurrency and money laundering activities to fund them.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan police launch guidebook on tackling student issues
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
A NEW police guide aims to improve how school liaison officers address social issues among students through more structured briefings.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the initiative was discussed during a meeting with the state Education Department on improving information sharing between them.
He said the 'Buku Mesra', launched on July 9, was inspired by former deputy inspector-general of police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay.
"The book provides officers with guidance on student-related issues, including what should and should not be done during briefings. It ensures the information provided is appropriate and easy for students to understand."
Previously, officers gave briefings based on specific topics, he said, adding that the new approach would be more targeted through closer coordination with the Education Department.
He said briefings would be conducted at suitable times, including during school hours, with content tailored to students' age groups and education levels.
Briefings may be grouped by age, such as pupils from Year One to Year Three, subject to the Education Department's approval.
He said sexual harassment was among issues requiring urgent attention, as many students might not fully understand what it involved.
The initiative will also strengthen cooperation between the police and the Education Department to prevent social problems through early intervention.

Title: Nestle Malaysia outpaces 2025 emissions target
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd has cut its greenhouse gas emissions by 31 per cent from its 2018 baseline.
This surpasses its interim target of a 20 per cent reduction by 2025, advancing towards its goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.
Nestle Malaysia said the achievement was driven by initiatives across its operations and supply chain.
This includes the transition to 100 per cent renewable electricity, manufacturing efficiency improvements, regenerative agriculture, sustainable sourcing practices and circular packaging programmes.
Nestle Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the milestone reflects years of collaboration across the company's operations and value chain.
"Reaching a 31 per cent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions is an important milestone, reflecting years of commitment by our teams and partners across Malaysia.
"While we are proud of this progress, we know there is still much more to do on our journey to net zero," he said.
Aranols said sustainability remains integral to the company's operations, from energy use and sourcing practices to packaging, ecosystem restoration and community initiatives.
The gas emission reduction milestone was unveiled during the company's "Nestle: Sustainability, Connected" event, which highlighted sustainability initiatives across its value chain.
The announcement also comes as Malaysia advances its climate commitments under its Nationally Determined Contribution, submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change in October 2025, which outlines the country's pathway towards net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050.
Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said private sector participation will be crucial in achieving Malaysia's climate goals.
"Initiatives, such as those undertaken by Nestle Malaysia, show that emissions reductions can be integrated into business operations while supporting long-term economic growth," he said.
Nestle Malaysia reaffirmed its focus on packaging sustainability through measures, such as reducing virgin plastic use, increasing recycled PET content and strengthening post-consumer waste recovery.
A key initiative is Nestle Kitar, the refreshed platform for Project SAVE (Segregate, Avoid, Value, Educate), which the company said is Malaysia's largest extended producer responsibility programme.
To date, the programme has recovered and recycled 50,000 tonnes of dry mixed waste, including 32,000 tonnes of plastics.
The company's sustainability efforts also extend to environmental restoration, with three million trees already planted nationwide under Project RELeaf.
Nestle Malaysia has committed to planting another three million trees by 2030 to support biodiversity conservation and climate resilience.
Having exceeded its 2025 emissions target, the company is now focused on achieving a 50 per cent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 as part of its pathway towards net zero by 2050.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump attorney-general pick looks set to clear US Senate hurdle
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's former personal lawyer Todd Blanche appeared on track on Monday to become the next US attorney-general after two Republican senators dropped their opposition to his nomination.
Blanche's Senate confirmation has been held up by concerns from Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis over a US$1.8 billion fund for alleged victims of politically motivated prosecution and a tax audit immunity deal with the Republican president.
Blanche issued a written order over the weekend scrapping the so-called "anti-weaponisation fund" and said the audit immunity agreement with Trump, his two eldest sons and the Trump Organization would apply only "retroactively" to past tax years and not future filings.
Cornyn and Tillis, both of whom are leaving the Senate in January, welcomed Blanche's moves in a statement on Monday and said they "look forward to voting to advance his nomination out of the Senate Judiciary Committee soon".
A vote in the committee, where Republicans hold a narrow 12-10 majority, is scheduled for Tuesday and the full Republican-controlled Senate is expected to weigh in on Blanche's nomination later in the week.
Senate Democrats are united in their opposition to Blanche's nomination amid concerns that he has treated the Department of Justice as an extension of the president's legal team.
"Senate Republicans are once again taking Trump's personal attorney at his word," Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said. "Blanche's so-called 'deal' does nothing, nothing to stop the (Internal Revenue Service) sweetheart deal that lets Trump and his family cheat their way out of tens of millions of dollars in taxes."
Blanche has also come in for criticism from victims of Jeffrey Epstein over his handling of the release of investigative files about the convicted sex offender, a one-time close friend of Trump.
Blanche, who has served as acting attorney general since Trump fired Pam Bondi in April, has overseen prosecutions of presidential adversaries and helped negotiate the extraordinary legal settlement between Trump and the government he controls.
The out-of-court settlement stems from Trump's US$10 billion lawsuit against the IRS over the illegal disclosure of his tax records by an agency contractor.
It proposed immunity from audits for past tax years and a US$1.776 billion fund for people who say they were unfairly targeted by the Department of Justice, potentially including Trump supporters convicted over the Jan 6, 2021 attack on the US Capitol.
'THERE IS NO FUND'
Federal judges have separately blocked the fund and condemned the tax settlement, which, according to US press reports, could help the president avoid past liabilities of up to US$100 million.
One judge ruled that Trump's lawsuit against the IRS had been brought for an "improper purpose" and sought to use the courts to legitimise benefits unavailable to ordinary taxpayers.
In his Sunday statement, Blanche said the "Order establishing the Anti-Weaponization Fund is rescinded and shall have no force or effect".
"This Order establishes, beyond any doubt, that there is no Fund," it said.
Blanche has been closely tied to what Democrats have dubbed a "retribution" campaign by the president against his perceived political enemies.
Former FBI director James Comey, an outspoken Trump critic, is among those who have been targeted under Blanche. Comey was indicted in April for allegedly threatening Trump's life in an Instagram post.
Prior to joining the Department of Justice, Blanche represented Trump in his New York trial over alleged "hush money" paid to porn star Stormy Daniels.
He was also on the legal defence team in two federal cases brought against Trump by special counsel Jack Smith — for allegedly mishandling classified documents after leaving the White House and for seeking to overturn the results of the 2020 presidential election.
Both cases were dropped after Trump won the 2024 presidential election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says talks with Iran under way but Teheran denies any planned
Article:
WASHINGTON/DUBAI: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that talks with Iran were under way, warning that it was a "last chance" for Teheran to sign a good deal to end the five-month-old war, but Iran denied that any negotiations were being held or planned.
The contradictory statements suggest there is little prospect of a diplomatic resolution to the war any time soon.
"They are going on right now," Trump told reporters at an Oval Office event when asked about the state of negotiations, saying the sides were talking at the request of Iran, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar, among others.
"This is a last chance for them (Iran) to sign a good document," he said.
Trump's comments followed his decision this weekend to call off what he said would be "massive attacks" he had authorised on Iran, saying talks were to be held, repeating a pattern in which he has vowed major strikes only to cancel them.
Earlier on Monday, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said no negotiations with the United States were taking place and no meetings were scheduled. Iran had no plans to host foreign delegations or send negotiators abroad in the coming days, he said.
Baghaei added that all Iranian negotiators were currently in the country, apart from Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi, who was on a religious pilgrimage in Iraq. The only talks under way, he said, were discussions with Oman over the management of the Strait of Hormuz.
A senior Iranian source also told Reuters that no talks were planned and that Araqchi would be unavailable at least until the end of the week.
Gulf officials and analysts said Iran is betting it can outlast Washington by turning the Middle East's trade routes, shipping lanes and energy infrastructure into pressure points that steadily raise the cost of confrontation, hoping to convince the United States and its allies that containing the crisis is more costly than accommodating Iran's demands over the Strait of Hormuz.
[[nid:1503598]]
"Their big advantage is that they can hurt the regional states and the global economy," said Michael Knights of the Washington Institute.
In a post on Truth Social later on Monday, Trump called Iran's leadership "unbelievably duplicitous", saying they had asked for a meeting and more talks were scheduled for the "immediate future".
He also repeated his assertion that the US Navy had total control over the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flowed before the conflict.
"'The United States Wall of Steel!' Nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a Deal, or Total Surrender, is accomplished," he wrote.
REPEATED PATTERN
Monday's developments appeared to fit a pattern that has emerged since Trump launched "Operation Epic Fury" alongside Israel more than five months ago. On several occasions, Trump has threatened military action only to later cite diplomatic contacts as a reason for stepping back.
[[nid:1503597]]
Iran, however, has publicly rejected negotiations with Washington since a June memorandum of understanding aimed at ending the conflict collapsed in early July.
Trump has yet to achieve the objectives he set out at the outset of the war: dismantling Iran's nuclear programme, curbing its ability to attack regional rivals and creating conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers.
Repeated US escalations have been met by escalating Iranian responses against US forces in the region, Washington's Gulf Arab allies and shipping, each time ending with Trump stepping back.
The dispute over the Strait of Hormuz remains a central point of contention. Washington says the June memorandum required Iran to open the strategically vital waterway, while Teheran argues the text explicitly preserved its authority over shipping traffic.
That would leave Teheran with greater leverage over the strait than before the war, a result that would likely be seen as a significant setback for Trump.
So far, the United States has failed to compel Iran to relinquish its grip on the waterway, sending global oil prices higher and pushing up politically sensitive petrol prices in the United States.
Amid signs that US-Iran tensions were easing again, oil prices dropped and major stock indexes gained on Monday. Brent crude futures fell about 7 per cent to around US$83.77 a barrel, while the Dow registered a record closing high.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australia confirms first mass death of seabirds from H5N1
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
AUSTRALIA warned yesterday against the risk of a wider spread of H5N1 bird flu after its first mass mortality episode among seabirds killed about 50 greater crested terns off the coast south of Adelaide.
However, there is no evidence yet of the virus on Australia's farms, many of which have locked down to safeguard poultry flocks since it was first detected in June.
Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said testing confirmed H5N1 bird flu in a group of 49 dead and 35 sick terns found by helicopter surveillance on rocks off Cape Jaffa, 250km from Adelaide last Friday.
"Australians should expect to see more spread and larger numbers now of wildlife being affected," she said here.
"This is the first confirmed case of a mass mortality," she added. "Once the H5 bird flu is spreading in wildlife and the natural environment, it is not possible to avoid significant losses, which is what we're starting to see now."
Australia's tally of 74 confirmed cases was spread as wide as the states of Western Australia and Queensland, though most cases were in South Australia, said Collins.
Australia and New Zealand, which saw its first H5N1 case last month, have spent years bracing for the virus, with steps such as tighter biosecurity at farms, testing of shore birds, vaccinating vulnerable species and war-gaming response plans.
H5N1 bird flu can infect humans who have contact with infected animals. But the number of cases worldwide is small and officials say the risk to humans is low. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aston Martin creditors threaten legal action over plan to sell branding rights
Article:
MEXICO CITY: A group of Aston Martin's creditors has threatened legal action against the carmaker after learning that it plans to sell a portion of its branding and naming rights as part of a new debt financing package, the Financial Times reported on Monday.
The loss-making luxury carmaker secured £550 million (US$738.38 million) in debt financing in July, led by funds managed by BlackRock-owned HPS Investment Partners.
The financing comprises a £450 million secured term loan, a £100 million delayed-draw term loan and a separate £100 million permitted debt-incurrence capacity.
Some existing creditors owed £1.3 billion sent a "letter before action" to the debt-laden British company's board on Sunday, warning they could seek to unwind the HPS transaction and block the disposal of certain intellectual property assets, the FT report said, without identifying the creditors.
Aston Martin and HPS could not immediately be reached for comment outside regular business hours. Reuters could not independently verify the report.
The creditors have learned that part of the deal depends on the carmaker transferring a 50.1 per cent stake in its non-automotive intellectual property to US brand developer Authentic Brands, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter.
The additional £100 million under the HPS financing package is conditional on the branding rights transaction taking place, according to the report. HPS is also an investor in Authentic Brands.
Aston Martin has refused to share details of its deal with HPS, leaving some creditors in the dark about the agreement, the FT report said.
Aston Martin has been grappling with cash pressures from weaker sales, US tariffs and soft demand in China, prompting the 113-year-old automaker to pursue cost cuts and fresh funding.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Death toll from Venezuela quakes rises past 6,000
Article:
CARACAS: The twin quakes that shattered Venezuela in June killed 6,125 people, National Assembly Chief Jorge Rodriguez said on Monday.
The updated figure comes weeks after the magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 quakes struck on June 24, causing nearly 200 buildings to collapse, mostly in the worst-hit coastal state of La Guaira.
The previous death toll stood at 5,546.
Rescue teams and family members continue to sift through the rubble in search of victims and loved ones, while almost 17,000 people were injured in the tremors.
Local media quoted La Guaira Governor Jose Alejandro Teran as saying around 1,400 people remain missing after the disaster.
The government has not otherwise disclosed how many people are missing, but expert projections have put the figure at up to 10,000.
In addition to 190 completely destroyed buildings, authorities have classified 6,433 structures as "high-risk", while another 9,866 have been designated as "restricted housing" to underline the dangers for inhabitants.
Almost 24,000 people in La Guaira and Caracas are living in makeshift shelters following the earthquakes.
Venezuelan lawmakers on Friday unanimously approved a law that makes it easier to rent properties.
The measure, aimed at helping displaced quake victims, must be enacted by interim leader Delcy Rodriguez to become law.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man's body found floating in river wrapped in net
Article:
BATU PAHAT: The body of a man believed to have been murdered was found floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, here yesterday.
It is learnt that the victim's bloated remains were found wrapped in a net.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani confirmed the discovery when contacted.
He said a statement on the discovery would be issued by the Johor police headquarters.
A post about the discovery of a man's body with his hands and legs tied and wrapped in a net went viral on social media.
The body was discovered by residents who initially mistook it for a livestock carcass before contacting the police.

Title: Loke blames slander, personal attacks for Chennah defeat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke blamed personal attacks and slander as among the reasons for his failure to defend the Chennah seat in the Negri Sembilan election.
Loke, who lost the Chennah seat by about 600 votes, described the contest and campaigning for the Aug 1 polls as the toughest challenge of his 22-year electoral career.
He said unfounded allegations were seized upon by his opponents to fuel a false narrative.
"There were parties who took the opportunity to portray me and DAP in a certain way — claiming that I wanted to become all sorts of things, control matters and take away Malay power.
"And in Negri Sembilan, particularly in the villages, these whispers proved effective," he said.
He was speaking to reporters at a press conference after a meeting of the party's Central Executive Committee (CEC).
Loke said the allegations had gained enough traction that some of his own voters approached him during the campaign to ask whether they were true.
"Many villagers asked me themselves — 'Is it true, YB, that you want to become Menteri Besar? Is it really true that YB is harbouring ambitions of becoming a Tok Undang?'
"These were questions from my own voters," he said.
Loke said the episode reflected what he described as political tactics, adding that even content framed as a joke had been used to create fear and suspicion among voters.
However, he maintained that this was part and parcel of politics and that he bore no ill will.
"This is the rough and tumble of politics. In the world of politics, one is indeed slandered and attacked from all sides.
"Unfortunately, I became a victim of all this defamation," he said.
Despite the defeat, Loke said contesting in Chennah was not a mistake, adding that he had demonstrated the courage expected of a party leader by taking on a difficult seat.
"As a leader and politician, I think I have shown courage and set an example that even though it was a tough seat, we took up the challenge.
"We die standing," he said.

Title: Maran Umno Youth chief on the way home from family getaway before accident
Article:
TEMERLOH: Maran Umno Youth chief Mohd Radzi Rahimi took part in a motorcycle convoy in Pulau Pangkor, Perak, before going on a family holiday to Genting Highlands yesterday.
His father, Rahimi Abd Samad, 63, said his eldest of four children travelled to Pulau Pangkor with his wife, Nuraini Mohammad Jafri, 36, and their 5-year-old twin sons last Thursday.
"I last met him on Thursday at my home in Taman Maran Jaya. He went to Pangkor to take part in a motorcycle convoy with a group of youths from Maran.
"After returning from Pangkor, I was informed that they decided to spend a night in Genting Highlands yesterday and were supposed to return to Maran today. I am not sure why they were travelling to Janda Baik today," he said when met at the Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas) forensic unit here today.
Rahimi said he was told that Radzi's wife, brother-in-law Mohammad Nizam Mohammad Jafri, and their sons travelled to Pangkor in a pick-up truck, while Radzi rode his motorcycle with the rest of the convoy.
"They met in Bentong yesterday when one of Radzi's friends took over riding the motorcycle. Radzi, his family and his brother-in-law then travelled to Genting Highlands for a short break," he said.
Rahimi said Radzi, a contractor, had continued the family's legacy in Umno after becoming actively involved in politics in Maran. He had served as the Maran Umno Youth chief for the past 2 years.
Radzi, 40, together with Nuraini, Nizam, 34, and his 5-year-old son, Muhammad Rizz Hazim Mohd Radzi, were killed after a
large
tree fell onto their pick-up truck along the old Kuala Lumpur-Bentong Road near Janda Baik at 12.30pm today.
His other 5-year-old twin son, Muhammad Rizz Haziq Mohd Radzi, was taken to Bentong Hospital before being
transferred
to Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas) for further treatment.
